The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the story, the narrative builds toward the inevitable reality of the father's illness and death, culminating in the emotional climax of the dance at the White Party. In that scene, the father explicitly asks his daughter to remember and tell their story in a specific way ("Don't let them tell you it was sad... Tell it right"). The final section provides a deep sense of closure by resolving the central premise—showing the father's passing, tying up the minor character threads (like Marcus, Eli, and the mother's laminated card), and circling back to the opening lines about the Windsor knot and the Negroni. By concluding with the narrator fulfilling her promise to her father, the story reaches the exact emotional and thematic resolution it was leading the reader toward from the very beginning.
